---
title: "5 · Ground states and unitary dynamics"
code-tools: false

![](../assets/thumbs/ch05.png){width=60% fig-align=center fig-alt="Ground states and unitary dynamics"}

Each method of this chapter has its own notebook. Spin Hamiltonians on arbitrary graphs are written as lists of
local terms, and the Lanczos algorithm, derived from the power method, delivers their ground states without
building a matrix. Three propagators follow: Trotter–Suzuki splitting with two-site gates (orders one, two and
four), the Chebyshev expansion of the propagator, and Krylov-subspace exponentiation with an a-posteriori error
bound. Each is derived, implemented with `jit` and `lax.scan`, and validated against exact evolution.

A head-to-head benchmark compares the integrators on accuracy and cost, and the final notebook uses them for the
physics of quantum quenches in spin chains: relaxation of the magnetisation, light cones, domain-wall melting,
entanglement growth and the Loschmidt echo.

## Notebooks in this chapter

::: {.nb-item}
[Hamiltonians and ground states — from the power method to Lanczos](../ch05_ground_states_and_unitary_dynamics/11_hamiltonians_and_ground_states.ipynb)

Spin Hamiltonians on arbitrary graphs as lists of local terms, the matrix-free product H|ψ⟩, and the Lanczos algorithm derived from the power method: Ritz values, loss of orthogonality, symmetry sectors, and the ground-state physics of the Ising and XXZ models up to N = 18–20 spins.
:::

::: {.nb-item}
[Time evolution I — TEBD: Trotter–Suzuki evolution of a state vector](../ch05_ground_states_and_unitary_dynamics/12_tebd_trotter_suzuki.ipynb)

Matrix-free Trotter–Suzuki (TEBD) time evolution with two-site gates applied by einsum: derivation of the 1st, 2nd and 4th order formulas, measured local and global error scaling, conserved quantities as diagnostics, gate fusion, and a jit + lax.scan implementation validated against exact evolution and free fermions.
:::

::: {.nb-item}
[Time evolution II — Chebyshev propagation](../ch05_ground_states_and_unitary_dynamics/13_chebyshev_propagation.ipynb)

The Chebyshev (Tal-Ezer–Kosloff) expansion of the propagator: Chebyshev polynomials, Bessel coefficients, the Jacobi–Anger identity, spectral rescaling, a lax.scan implementation accurate to machine precision, and its cost compared with TEBD.
:::

::: {.nb-item}
[Time evolution III — Krylov propagation and the integrator shoot-out](../ch05_ground_states_and_unitary_dynamics/14_krylov_and_integrator_comparison.ipynb)

Krylov-subspace (Lanczos) exponentiation derived and validated, with a rigorous a-posteriori error bound and adaptive steps; then a measured head-to-head benchmark of exact, TEBD (orders 1, 2, 4), Chebyshev and Krylov integrators and a practical guide to choosing among them.
:::

::: {.nb-item}
[Quench dynamics in spin chains — light cones, entanglement growth, relaxation](../ch05_ground_states_and_unitary_dynamics/15_quench_dynamics_spin_chains.ipynb)

The time-evolution toolbox applied to quantum quenches in XXZ, Heisenberg and transverse-field Ising chains — relaxation of magnetisation, Lieb–Robinson light cones, domain-wall melting, entanglement growth, integrable versus non-integrable behaviour and the Loschmidt echo.
:::
